property_summary: For any caller and any _unlockTime, calling Put(...) sets the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime to be at least block.timestamp (i.e., not earlier than current block time); the mutant treating _unlockTime as a delay can set unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs (when _unlockTime is 0 in reference it sets to now, but mutant sets to now+_unlockTime which is >= now — actually mutant difference: reference sets max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) so it's >= block.timestamp; mutant sets block.timestamp + _unlockTime which can overflow? Correction: the real observable difference is that in reference calling Put with a past _unlockTime results in unlockTime == block.timestamp, while mutant sets unlockTime = block.timestamp + _unlockTime which for small _unlockTime may be equal or greater; the failing case is when _unlockTime is less than block.timestamp in P results in unlockTime == block.timestamp, while in M unlockTime becomes block.timestamp + _unlockTime which is greater than block.timestamp, so the rule chosen here: After Put, Acc[msg].unlockTime is >= block.timestamp and equals block.timestamp when the provided _unlockTime is <= block.timestamp; the mutant breaks this because it treats _unlockTime as a delay and will make unlockTime > block.timestamp for such inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime equals either the provided _unlockTime when that is in the future, or block.timestamp when the provided _unlockTime is in the past or zero (i.e., Acc[caller].unlockTime == (_unlockTime > block.timestamp ? _unlockTime : block.timestamp)); the mutant that treats _unlockTime as a delay (acc.unlockTime = block.timestamp + _unlockTime) will violate this for inputs where _unlockTime <= block.timestamp (it will set a value > block.timestamp).

For any caller and any _unlockTime, after Put(_unlockTime) the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime equals (_unlockTime > block.timestamp ? _unlockTime : block.timestamp); the mutant that treats _unlockTime as a delay (acc.unlockTime = block.timestamp + _unlockTime) violates this for inputs where _unlockTime <= block.timestamp.

After calling Put(u) from any sender, the stored Acc[sender].unlockTime equals (_unlockTime > block.timestamp ? _unlockTime : block.timestamp); the mutant that treats _unlockTime as a delay (acc.unlockTime = block.timestamp + _unlockTime) breaks this for inputs where _unlockTime <= block.timestamp.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime is never less than block.timestamp and, if the provided _unlockTime is <= block.timestamp, the stored unlockTime equals block.timestamp (the mutant that treats _unlockTime as a delay sets a strictly greater unlockTime for such inputs and thus violates this rule).

For any caller and any _unlockTime and deposit value, after Put returns the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is at least the current block.timestamp (i.e., non-decreasing relative to now); the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can violate intended behaviour when caller supplies a future _unlockTime (making stored unlockTime smaller than the requested future time).

For any caller, when calling Put with a future _unlockTime (> block.timestamp) the contract stores Acc[msg].unlockTime >= _unlockTime (i.e., preserves or extends requested future unlock), whereas the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can make stored unlockTime < _unlockTime for such inputs.

For any caller and any deposit value and requested _unlockTime, after calling Put the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is >= min(block.timestamp, _unlockTime) (i.e., it never sets the stored unlockTime earlier than the current block.timestamp or earlier than a requested past time); the mutant that forces acc.unlockTime = block.timestamp can violate this when a caller requests a future _unlockTime (> block.timestamp) because the mutant will set a smaller unlockTime than requested.

For any caller and any deposit amount and requested _unlockTime, if _unlockTime is strictly in the future (> block.timestamp) then after Put returns the stored Acc[msg].unlockTime equals that future _unlockTime (the reference preserves a requested future unlock time); the mutant that overwrites with block.timestamp will break this for some future _unlockTime inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, calling Put stores Acc[msg].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (i.e., the contract never sets a stored unlockTime earlier than now); the mutant that always sets acc.unlockTime = block.timestamp can violate this when a caller calls Put via a contract that advances block.timestamp before Put executes (so the reference can record a future _unlockTime but the mutant will store the then-current block.timestamp, making stored unlockTime < caller's supplied future value).

For all callers and input _unlockTime, calling Put(...) sets the caller's stored unlockTime to at least the current block.timestamp (i.e. acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp); the mutant that assigns _unlockTime directly can set acc.unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any Put(_unlockTime) call, the reference contract ensures the stored unlockTime for that caller is never less than the current block.timestamp (it uses max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that assigns _unlockTime directly can make stored unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any Put(_unlockTime) call, the reference ensures after Put that acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it stores max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that directly assigns _unlockTime can make acc.unlockTime < block.timestamp when _unlockTime is in the past, so the property is that acc.unlockTime is never less than block.timestamp after Put.

For any caller and any Put(_unlockTime) call, the reference C ensures that the stored unlockTime for that caller is at least the provided _unlockTime if _unlockTime is in the future, otherwise it sets it to the current block.timestamp — equivalently, the stored unlockTime is never less than the minimum of block.timestamp and the provided _unlockTime; the mutant that assigns _unlockTime directly can make the stored unlockTime strictly less than block.timestamp when _unlockTime is in the past, violating this relationship.

After any Put(...) call, the reference contract guarantees that the stored unlockTime for msg.sender is never less than the previous unlockTime OR the current block.timestamp (it never moves strictly earlier than either), while the mutant that assigns _unlockTime directly can decrease a holder's unlockTime to a past value causing acc.unlockTime to become less than its previous value and less than block.timestamp.

For any caller and any Put(value, unlockTime) call that sends a non-negative ether amount, the reference contract always updates the caller's Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime to max(unlockTime, block.timestamp) (so unlockTime >= block.timestamp after Put), whereas the mutant leaves unlockTime unchanged, so there exist inputs where unlockTime in the mutant is less than in the reference (breaking this rule).

After any Put call that may send ether, the reference contract ensures Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it sets unlockTime = max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)), whereas the mutant fails to update unlockTime so there exist inputs where Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp (breaking this invariant).

After any Put call by an address that sends a positive value, the reference C always sets Acc[caller].unlockTime to at least the block.timestamp or the provided _unlockTime (whichever is greater); the mutant that omits updating unlockTime can leave Acc[caller].unlockTime lower than block.timestamp or lower than the provided _unlockTime for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any inputs, after calling Put(...) (possibly sending ETH) the reference contract sets Acc[caller].unlockTime to at least block.timestamp or the provided _unlockTime (whichever is greater); the mutant that deletes the assignment to acc.unlockTime can leave Acc[caller].unlockTime unchanged and thus smaller than the required value for some inputs.

For any caller and any Put(uint _unlockTime) call (with any payable amount), the reference C always updates Acc[caller].unlockTime to be at least block.timestamp (specifically max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that omits the assignment can leave Acc[caller].unlockTime unchanged, so there exist inputs where the mutant's unlockTime is less than the reference's, violating this rule.

After any Put call from an address sending some value, the last log entry recorded by the contract's LogFile History should have Data == "Put"; the mutant changes the recorded Data string (e.g. to "Put_mutant") and thus breaks this property for some inputs.

For any caller and amount, after calling Put(...) the LogFile.History last entry's Data equals "Put" (the reference always logs "Put"; the mutant logs "Put_mutant" for some inputs and so violates this), and we detect that by checking the Last message stored in LogFile via its public History getter.

For every caller and value, after calling Put(...) the Log contract's History array grows by exactly one and that new entry's Val equals the ether sent; the mutant only changes the Data string but still must record the correct sender and value — however altering the Data breaks the general rule if we instead assert that the recorded Data starts with "Put" (the reference records "Put"; the mutant records "Put_mutant" and thus fails for inputs), so we assert the History last entry's Data has prefix "Put".

For every caller and value, calling Put records a log History entry whose Data string is exactly "Put" (the reference always logs "Put"; the mutant sometimes logs a different string like "Put_mutant" and thus violates this), and we detect this by reading the public LogFile.History last entry after Put.

For every caller and value, after calling Put(...) the external Log contract's last History entry Data equals the exact string "Put"; the mutant changes that string to "Put_mutant" so this equality is violated for some inputs.

A holder cannot withdraw exactly at the unlock time (Collect should fail when block.timestamp == unlockTime), so after depositing and setting unlockTime = T, calling Collect for amount >= MinSum at time T must not transfer funds.

Collect must not revert (reverted == false) when caller's unlockTime is strictly less than or equal to current block time only in the original but the mutant reverts when equal; we assert that if blockTimestamp >= unlockTime then Collect should revert (reverted == true).
If deposit >= c.MinSum() and withdraw <= deposit and block.timestamp == unlockTime then Collect must revert (reverted == true).
If deposit >= c.MinSum() && withdraw <= deposit && block.timestamp == unlockTime then Collect call reverts (reverted == true).
If deposit >= c.MinSum() and withdraw <= deposit and block.timestamp == unlockTime then the Collect call must revert (reverted == true).

Rule: A holder may only successfully Collect when block.timestamp is strictly greater than their unlockTime; the mutant that changes '>' to '>=' allows collection when block.timestamp == unlockTime, so there exist inputs (timing equal to unlockTime) where the mutant behaves differently.

The reference contract only allows a user to successfully Collect when the current block.timestamp is strictly greater than their recorded unlockTime; the mutant changing '>' to '>=' permits collection when timestamp == unlockTime, so there exist inputs (timestamp equal to unlockTime) where the mutant allows a Collect that the reference disallows.

For any depositor, calling Collect(amount) at block.timestamp equal to their unlockTime must revert (reference requires block.timestamp > unlockTime); the mutant using '>=' allows Collect to succeed when timestamp == unlockTime, violating this rule.

For any depositor, calling Collect(amount) when block.timestamp == their unlockTime must NOT succeed on the reference (it either does nothing or reverts/doesn't send funds); the mutant that changes '>' to '>=' can succeed and transfer funds at timestamp == unlockTime, so there exist inputs (deposit amount, withdrawal amount, and a warp to equal unlockTime) where the mutant allows a successful Collect but the reference does not.

For any depositor, calling Collect(amount) when block.timestamp == their stored unlockTime must NOT result in a successful withdrawal on the reference contract (it requires strictly greater), but the mutant that changes '>' to '>=' can succeed at timestamp == unlockTime, so there exist inputs (deposit amount, withdrawal amount, timing) where mutant allows success and reference does not.
If an account's recorded balance is below MinSum then calling Collect cannot transfer any ETH out (address(c).balance does not decrease).

property_summary: If caller's recorded balance is less than MinSum then Collect must not revert (i.e., original allows Collect to return normally), so reverted == false whenever caller's balance < MinSum and other numeric params are valid.

If the caller's recorded balance is less than MinSum but >= requested amount and unlock time passed, original Collect returns normally (no revert) while the mutant may revert; so for such inputs reverted must be false on the original behavior.
If callerReportedBalance >= am and callerReportedBalance < c.MinSum() then calling c.Collect(am) should not revert (reverted == false).
If the provided callerReportedBalance is at least am and strictly less than c.MinSum(), then calling c.Collect(am) should not revert (i.e., reverted == false).
